standard_prerequisites.name: Duality for a proper curve
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Serre duality on a proper scheme of dimension 1 over a field: H^1(X, F) is dual to Hom(F, omega_X), used with Lemma lemma-vanishing-on-gorenstein and the deg-chi formula
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the dimension identity dim H^0(X, IL) = deg(L) + chi(O_X) > dim H^0(X, omega_X) that forces the chosen map phi to vanish on global sections.

standard_prerequisites.name: Behaviour of global generation and genus under base field extension
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Varieties, Lemmas varieties-lemma-globally-generated-base-change, varieties-lemma-degree-base-change, varieties-lemma-geometrically-reduced-any-base-change, varieties-lemma-bijection-irreducible-components; Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma coherent-lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology
standard_prerequisites.use: Justifies replacing the ground field k by a purely transcendental extension K, so the union-of-subspaces argument may assume k infinite.

core_obligations: Reduce to an infinite ground field by a purely transcendental extension K/k (proof lines 5782-5792), and induct on the number of irreducible components; the irreducible case is Lemma lemma-degree-more-than-2g applied over k' = H^0(X, O_X).

Assume L not globally generated and pick a coherent ideal I with H^0(X, IL) = H^0(X, L) and O_X/I supported in dimension 0 (proof lines 5797-5821); the boundary map of 0 -> IL -> L -> L/IL -> 0 then injects H^0(X, L/IL) into H^1(X, IL).

Duality turns Hom(IL, omega_X) into the dual of H^1(X, IL); the strict inequality dim H^0(X, IL) > dim H^1(X, O_X) = dim H^0(X, omega_X) (proof lines 5833-5843) shows the union of the subspaces V_eta of maps vanishing at a generic point eta covers all of Hom(IL, omega_X), and since k is infinite one V_eta is everything (proof lines 5844-5860).

For that eta with component C and complement Y, every phi factors as IL -> IL/JIL -> omega_Y -> omega_X through I'L|_Y (proof lines 5863-5920 with the two commutative diagrams); the representing property of omega_X makes H^1(X, IL) -> H^1(Y, I'L|_Y) injective, and composing with the injective boundary map gives an injection H^0(X, L|_Y/I'L|_Y) -> H^1(X, I'L|_Y), contradicting global generation of L|_Y by induction, which makes the boundary map non-injective (proof lines 5920-5960).
proof_roadmap: Induct on irreducible components; base case = the irreducible lemma over H^0(X, O_X).
Replace k by a purely transcendental K; list the five base-change lemmas that keep all hypotheses intact.
Contradiction setup: ideal I with equal H^0 and 0-dimensional support; boundary injection into H^1(X, IL).
Duality dimension count plus infinity of K collapses Hom(IL, omega_X) to maps vanishing at one generic point eta.
Factor every phi through Y = X - C, transport to I'L|_Y, and read the contradiction off the boundary map for L|_Y.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves a global generation criterion by degree (statement lines 5754-5765: deg(L|_Y) >= 2 dim H^1(Y, O_Y) for every reduced connected closed Y of dimension 1). The proof (lines 5767-5919 and its closing lines to 5960) is not a single reference: it combines a base-field replacement, a duality dimension count dim H^0(X, IL) = deg(L) + chi(O_X) > dim H^0(X, omega_X), a generic-point union-of-subspaces argument that needs k infinite, a factorization of every Hom(IL, omega_X) through the complement Y via omega_Y = SheafHom(O_Y, omega_X), and a final boundary-map injectivity contradiction with the induction hypothesis. H3: several independent non-formal ingredients are composed, and the reduction step to infinite fields is itself a real argument.
